line_name: Direction de l'État Civil et Casier Judiciaire
purpose: `ANNEXE VI` prints the service as **« Direction de L'Etat Civil et Casier Judiciaire »** (capitalisation as printed) under `06 MINISTERE DE LA JUSTICE, DES AFFAIRES ISLAMIQUES ET DE LA FONCTION PUBLIQUE`, and states no purpose beyond the label.

The directorate is the institutional custodian of the Comorian civil register and criminal record — the population register — and is the only line at any grain in any of the three country-years that funds it. **The appropriation names no digital activity**, so the scope claim rests on the body's mandate rather than on the line's stated purpose; recorded `unclear` and flagged rather than asserted as `whole`.

Proved by the annexe's own arithmetic: the ministry's five service totals sum to **235 315 816** in the `LFA 2025` column and **682 681 240** in the `LFR 2024` column, both matching `Article 11` of the enacted law and of the native PLF to the franc. ⚠ The *Budget Citoyen 2025* prints the same table in **millions KMF** (`235`) — read the header per artefact.

notes: ⚠ This is the first identity-and-data-exchange line the Comorian corpus holds, and it corrects a standing three-year finding.** All three sweeps recorded that no line exists at any grain for a population register, CRVS, national identity card, biometric enrolment, passport system, voter register or social registry. One does: the civil-registry and criminal-record directorate, at service grain, in the FY2025 and FY2026 classifications. What the sweeps got right is that **no line names a digital or registry-modernisation activity** — this one funds the registry's ordinary running, in goods and services only. · KMF 3 000 000 is about €6 100 a year.** No salary line, no capital line, ever. Against that: France finances *Appui à la modernisation de l'état civil aux Comores — AMECC*, which appears in the FY2026 law's own public-investment programme annexe; the AMECC civil-registry digitisation study for Mohéli ran in October 2025; and the state's revenue tables book **324 000 000 KMF of *Recettes des documents d'État Civil*** for FY2026 and **2 866 000 000 KMF of *Timbres fiscaux (Documents Biométriques Semlex)***. **The registry raises roughly 1 000 times what it is appropriated to spend, and its modernisation is entirely donor-financed.** · `released`, `actual` and `audited` stages uncovered for FY2025** as at 2026-08-04. · `amount_usd` left blank** — no named fiscal-year-average KMF rate is held.

All three sweeps missed it because the Comorian classification is by economic nature and no keyword search of the *amounts* reaches it; the service **name** is the handle, and it has to be read off the classification's designation column. · The scale of it, FY2025: 9 128 000 KMF — about €18 600 a year** to run the computing directorate of a state whose finance ministry was simultaneously tendering for two datacentres, LAN/WLAN, firewalls, IPS, SIEM and two network operations centres under the AFD-financed PAGF-SI project. The gap between what the fisc appropriates and what donors buy is the whole story of Comorian digital spend, and this line is the sharpest single measurement of it. · Then the rectificative zeroed it, and the FY2026 law appropriates 277 128 000** — thirty times the FY2025 figure and 82% of the entire digital ministry's FY2026 vote.
